posts.title: An open letter of thanks to Gail Miller
posts.description: Donna Barnes | Lehi Free Press I became somewhat acquainted with the Larry Miller Family in 2002. My family had always been a family of softball players, and we knew of Larry Miller’s love of the game because of the teams he built in the 80s and 90s. A world championship was being held in Eau Claire, Wisconsin, and my 3 sons were playing together on a team that was invited to participate in the tourney. After much discussion, my husband and I decided to travel to Wisconsin. After a week of softball games, we headed home. We went to the front desk to pay our bill, only to be told the Miller team’s representative had already paid it. We were shocked and grateful. As our family continued to be part of the softball and baseball world, we became aware of the amazing amount of investment the Miller family had made in beautiful parks, the Cottonwood Complex, the Valley Complex, etc. One year my granddaughter’s Lehi High School softball team was to play West High School. posts.title: City leaders discuss retrofitting existing buildings for justice court, fire station
posts.description: Nichole Coombs | Lehi Free Press Renovate and reuse. That’s what council members Rachel Freeman and James Harrison hope to do to ease crowding at the Lehi Justice Court and Fire Station 81. “Council member Freeman had this idea back before we were sworn in,” said Harrison. “We met with the fire chief and Judge Cummings at the time and realized that the state of that whole building was pretty dire. We don’t have room for our firefighters to sleep, and the whole court is just getting busier.” Harrison says the Lehi Civic Center master plan calls for a new justice court to accommodate the court’s growing needs. “Rachel really was the one who asked if we could renovate the old city council chambers into a space for the justice court,” said Harrison. posts.title: Portion of APSD property in Lehi declared surplus, to be sold
posts.description: Megan Wallgren | Lehi Free Press The Aspen Peaks School Board declared a parcel of land in Lehi surplus property for disposition at its October 22 board meeting. The property, located at 7829-7753 S Center Street in Lehi, is currently owned by Alpine School District, but the title will pass to APSD by or before July 1, 2027. The parcel consists of approximately 4.9 acres and was deemed “no longer needed for district operations of Alpine School District (“ASD”) and will not be needed for the operation of Aspen Peaks School District (“APSD”).” The land is part of a larger parcel owned by the district with Parcel ID: 13:034:85. Much of the parcel, including the remaining 9.46 acres along Center Street and Pioneer Crossing, will remain under district ownership.
